stories.head: Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closed 'further day by day'
stories.say: Iran's army chief says the Strait of Hormuz will be closed further day by day until Washington meets seven conditions, as Qatar's prime minister tries to revive talks in Washington.
stories.stand: Iran's military says the strait will tighten until the US meets seven conditions, while Qatar's prime minister lobbies Washington to restart talks.
body: Iran's army commander-in-chief, Major General Amir Hatami, said on Monday that the navy would keep closing the Strait of Hormuz further day by day. He said seven Iranian conditions must be met before it reopens.

The Revolutionary Guards said three oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire on Monday. A joint maritime information centre has said earlier mine claims were unconfirmed, and the tanker reports have not been independently verified.

Qatar's prime minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, met Marco Rubio and JD Vance in Washington on Monday. He said the region could not bear renewed escalation and that Doha was working to bring both sides back to talks.

stories.head: Ukraine says it struck Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland
stories.say: Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukrainian sea drones struck the Russian cargo ship Sparta Two in the Gulf of Finland. Norway says it is talking to Kyiv about stability in the region.
stories.stand: Zelenskyy called the sanctioned ship a legitimate target, as NATO neighbours voice unease about the war spreading beyond Ukraine.
body: Ukraine says it attacked the Russian cargo ship Sparta II in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, setting it on fire. The ship belongs to Oboronlogistika, which provides logistics for Russia's defence ministry and has been under US sanctions since 2022.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said seven domestically made naval drones were used and that the ship was a legitimate military target. Russian authorities said on Tuesday the ship had been towed back to a Russian port.

Norway's defence minister, Tore Sandvik, said on Tuesday that Oslo was talking to Kyiv about the need for stability in the region. The Kremlin accused Ukraine's allies of letting it use their territory for strikes.

stories.head: Car bomb injures at least 24 in Colombian city of Villavicencio
stories.say: A car bomb has injured at least twenty-four people in the Colombian city of Villavicencio. The president blamed narco-terrorism and said he would not negotiate with criminals.
stories.stand: No group has claimed the blast, which damaged a regional government building in central Colombia.
body: A car bomb exploded in Villavicencio, the capital of Colombia's Meta department, on Monday, injuring at least 24 people, according to authorities. The blast damaged a regional government headquarters and nearby buildings.

President Abelardo de la Espriella visited the city on Tuesday and blamed what he called narco-terrorism. He said he would not back down or negotiate with criminals. No group has claimed responsibility.
The mayor, Alexander Baquero, imposed a temporary ban on motorcycles on several main roads. Local authorities offered a reward of up to 150 million pesos, around €38,000, for information.

stories.head: Sheikh Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh on 16 December
stories.say: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's exiled former prime minister, says she will fly home from India on the sixteenth of December. The government says she can only return through extradition.
stories.stand: The ex-leader, sentenced to death in absentia, wants the government to fly her home; ministers say she must be extradited.
body: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's former prime minister, plans to return from exile in India on 16 December, her spokesperson said on Tuesday. She asked the government to arrange a flight from Delhi to Dhaka.
A tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia over the crackdown on the 2024 uprising that ended her 15-year rule. The UN says as many as 1,400 people were killed in that unrest.
The prime minister's press secretary, Abu Abdullah M Saleh, said she could return only through extradition as a convicted person. She is expected to be arrested if she arrives.

stories.head: Malaysia plans to send more than 6,500 Rohingya back to Myanmar
stories.say: Malaysia's prime minister Anwar Ibrahim says more than six thousand five hundred Rohingya refugees will be returned to Myanmar in December, by navy ship and by plane.
stories.stand: Anwar Ibrahim told parliament Malaysia can no longer afford to host refugees; rights groups have criticised earlier returns.
body: Malaysia's prime minister, Anwar Ibrahim, told parliament on Tuesday that more than 6,500 Rohingya refugees would be returned to Myanmar. He said Malaysia could no longer afford to host refugees.
He said 1,500 people would travel on three navy vessels in early December, and 5,303 by aircraft paid for by Myanmar's government. About 1,500 migrants were already sent back in late September.
Rights groups have criticised the earlier returns. Malaysia said in October it would seek clarification of reports that returnees were detained by Myanmar's military.

stories.head: Solomon Islands to let China security pact lapse as Australia deal nears
stories.say: Solomon Islands will not renew its security pact with China, according to Australia's ABC, as Prime Minister Matthew Wale arrives in Canberra to sign a treaty worth nearly a billion dollars.
stories.stand: Matthew Wale is in Canberra to sign a treaty with Australia; Beijing has reportedly been told the 2022 pact will not be renewed.
body: Solomon Islands has told China that its 2022 security pact will not be renewed when it expires in April next year, according to ABC sources. Nine Newspapers reported that Honiara had told Beijing it would withdraw.
Prime Minister Matthew Wale arrived in Canberra on Tuesday with a 24-strong delegation. He is due to sign a treaty with Australia that includes $980 million in additional funding.
Australia's foreign minister, Penny Wong, has called the 2022 agreement the worst foreign policy blunder in the Pacific since the Second World War. The Chinese embassy has not commented.

stories.head: South Korea issues shelter alert as Russian warplanes near Ulleungdo
stories.say: South Korea scrambled fighter jets and told residents of Ulleungdo island to take shelter on Tuesday, as Russian military aircraft entered its air defence zone before turning away.
stories.stand: The aircraft entered South Korea's air defence identification zone but did not violate its airspace, the military said.
body: South Korea scrambled fighter jets on Tuesday as Russian military aircraft approached the eastern island of Ulleungdo. Residents were told to take shelter, and the warning was lifted within minutes.
The Joint Chiefs of Staff said the aircraft entered the Korea Air Defence Identification Zone but did not violate territorial airspace. Yonhap reported they spent about 20 minutes in the zone.
The defence ministry summoned Russia's military attaché, Colonel Nikolai Marchenko, to protest. An early alert wrongly said the aircraft had entered South Korean airspace.

stories.head: Israeli strikes kill seven in Gaza including Hamas security chief
stories.say: Israeli air strikes have killed seven people in Gaza, Palestinian officials say, including the head of Hamas's internal security service. Israel said it hit a senior Hamas figure.
stories.stand: Palestinian officials say police officers and a teenager were among the dead, despite the ceasefire in place since October 2025.
body: Israeli air strikes killed at least seven people in Gaza on Tuesday, according to Palestinian health officials. Gaza's interior ministry said one strike killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, head of the Internal Security Service.
Israel's military said it struck a senior Hamas operative. Civil defence officials said a 17-year-old was among three killed near Gaza City, and three more died in a strike in Al-Mawasi.

Gaza's health ministry says more than 1,650 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began in October 2025. Israel's military says seven soldiers and a civilian contractor have died in that period.

stories.head: Indonesia names former police chief a treason suspect
stories.say: Indonesian police have named former national police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo as one of six treason suspects over alleged illegal surveillance of President Prabowo Subianto.
stories.stand: Police allege the wiretapping was part of a plot to undermine the government; the claims have not been tested in court.
body: Indonesian police have named former national police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo as one of six treason suspects, in a case over alleged illegal surveillance of President Prabowo Subianto.

The head of the police criminal investigation agency, Asep Safrudin, alleged that Listyo ordered the wiretapping and received the reports. Police also accused some suspects of organising anti-government protests.

Listyo was arrested on 3 November and dismissed as presidential chief of staff the next day. He faces a police ethics hearing on Thursday. The offences carry penalties up to life imprisonment or death.

stories.head: Shanghai party chief Chen Jining placed under investigation
stories.say: China has placed Shanghai's Communist Party chief, Chen Jining, under investigation for serious violations of discipline and law. He's the fourth Politburo member investigated this term.
stories.stand: The probe into a Politburo member once tipped for promotion is the latest in Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign.
body: China's top anti-corruption body is investigating Chen Jining, the Communist Party secretary of Shanghai, state media announced on Tuesday. He is accused of serious violations of discipline and law, a phrase usually used for corruption.
Chen is a member of the Politburo and was once widely tipped for a top leadership role. He has been Beijing's mayor, environment minister and president of Tsinghua University.
He is the fourth Politburo member investigated this term. No details of the allegations have been released.

stories.head: Leaked Rosstat data shows at least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed
stories.say: Leaked Russian statistics records suggest at least four hundred and ninety thousand Russian servicemen have died in the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin publishes no figures.
stories.stand: Hackers took the data from Russia's statistics agency; independent media say the real toll is likely higher.
body: Data taken from Russia's statistics agency, Rosstat, shows at least 490,000 Russian servicemen have been killed since February 2022, according to analysis reported by Euronews. The count is based on registered death certificates up to the end of August 2026.
The hacker groups Cyber Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow say they extracted the data on 1 November. The figure excludes missing soldiers and deaths that were never registered.
The Russian outlet Meduza estimates irrecoverable losses of at least 720,000, including the missing. The Kremlin does not publish its own casualty figures.

stories.head: Mexico to try 'El Chapo Isidro' at home despite US extradition request
stories.say: Mexico's attorney general says captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores will be put on trial in Mexico, even though the United States wants him extradited.
stories.stand: Mexico says US intelligence and surveillance drones helped track the alleged Sinaloa cartel leader, but no US forces operated on the ground.
body: Mexico will put alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', on trial at home, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said on Monday. The United States has asked for his extradition.
He was captured on Friday in Guasave, Sinaloa, after a firefight. Four soldiers and 16 suspected cartel gunmen were killed in the operation and the violence that followed, officials said.
Mexican officials said the US shared intelligence and Mexico authorised US surveillance drone flights. President Claudia Sheinbaum said US forces did not operate on the ground.

stories.head: Victims failed at every stage of the justice system, survey finds
stories.say: A survey of six thousand crime victims in England and Wales found nearly half were unhappy with how police kept in touch, and almost half of Crown Court cases were postponed.
stories.stand: The Victims' Commissioner says victims are too often treated as an afterthought; ministers point to £550 million in funding.
body: The Victim Survey 2026, based on responses from 6,000 victims in England and Wales, found 46% were dissatisfied with police communication. Of those whose cases reached Crown Court, 47% saw a postponement.
Only 14% knew their rights under the Victims' Code. Of those unhappy with police communication, 85% said they would not report a crime again.

Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman called for an end-to-end review. The victims minister, Alex Davies-Jones, cited £550 million for victim services over three years and said a new Victims' Code will be published next year.

stories.head: Met makes 266 arrests and seizes about 500 knives in week-long crackdown
stories.say: The Metropolitan Police says a week-long knife crime crackdown in London led to two hundred and sixty-six arrests and the removal of about five hundred knives.
stories.stand: The operation ran from 16 to 23 November; 175 knives were found at two addresses in east London alone.
body: The Metropolitan Police says a week-long knife crime operation across London from 16 to 23 November led to 266 arrests. It says about 500 knives were taken off the streets.

One suspect was charged after 175 knives were found at two addresses in east London, the force said. In south London, four men were charged with possessing offensive weapons after a stolen car was stopped.
The Met says knife crime offences fell 8.1% over the last 12 months. Commander James Conway said every knife seized could not be used to hurt someone.

stories.say: A Metropolitan Police pilot found that one in eight vapes seized from pupils at schools in south-west London contained illicit drugs, including THC and spice.
stories.stand: Officers tested 32 vapes with a specialist device; the force calls it an emerging threat to children.

stories.head: Court told former prince Andrew received £750,000 'bribe' in heiress case
stories.say: The High Court has heard claims that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor received seven hundred and fifty thousand pounds linked to a Turkish heiress. He isn't accused of wrongdoing.
stories.stand: Nebahat Isbilen is suing her former adviser Selman Turk, who denies the claims; Andrew is due to give evidence on 14 December.
body: A civil trial at the High Court heard claims on Monday that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor received £750,000 described as a bribe to help Turkish heiress Nebahat Isbilen. Isbilen, 81, is suing her former adviser Selman Turk.
She alleges Turk misappropriated tens of millions of pounds of her money and sent about £2 million to Alphabet Capital, some of which reached Andrew and Sarah Ferguson. Turk denies the allegations.
Andrew is not accused of wrongdoing and, according to Isbilen's submissions, returned the £750,000. A judge has allowed Turk to summon him, and he is due to testify on 14 December.

stories.head: Police seize 893kg of suspected cocaine hidden in boxes of oranges
stories.say: Police have seized eight hundred and ninety-three kilos of suspected cocaine, much of it hidden in boxes of oranges at New Spitalfields Market in east London. Eight men are in custody.
stories.stand: The Met says it is one of its biggest drug seizures; about £450,000 in cash was also found.
body: The Metropolitan Police says 893kg of suspected cocaine has been seized in an investigation that began with a find in boxes of oranges at New Spitalfields Market in Leyton on Sunday evening.

Eight men are in custody on suspicion of conspiracy to supply class A drugs, police said. About 250kg was found in a lorry stopped near Maidstone, and about £450,000 in cash at a property in Cheshunt.
Detective Superintendent Lindsey Billany said the seizure was a significant loss to the criminal enterprise. The investigation is continuing.

stories.head: Prisoner admits murdering Ian Huntley and gets second whole-life term
stories.say: Anthony Russell has admitted murdering the Soham killer Ian Huntley at Frankland prison, changing his plea on Tuesday. He was given a second whole-life sentence.
stories.stand: Russell, already serving a whole-life term for three murders, attacked Huntley with a metal bar in a prison workshop in February.
body: Anthony Russell, 44, changed his plea to guilty on Tuesday and admitted murdering Ian Huntley at HMP Frankland, near Durham. His trial had opened at Newcastle Crown Court on Monday.
Prosecutors said Russell struck Huntley at least six times with a 4kg metal bar in a prison workshop on 26 February. Huntley, 52, died nine days later.
Russell was given a second whole-life order. He was already serving one for three murders. Huntley was jailed in 2003 for the murders of Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman in Soham.

stories.head: Seventy firefighters tackle overnight blaze at Bexleyheath bingo hall
stories.say: About seventy firefighters tackled an overnight fire at a bingo hall and car park on Broadway in Bexleyheath, in south-east London. No injuries were reported.
stories.stand: London Fire Brigade said the fire, on three floors and a roof terrace, is believed to have been accidental.
body: About 70 firefighters and ten fire engines were called to a fire at a bingo hall and multi-storey car park on Broadway in Bexleyheath overnight. The first of six calls came at 01:57 and the fire was under control by 04:17.
Parts of the first, second and third floors and the roof terrace were alight, London Fire Brigade said. No injuries were reported.
Nearby residents were told to keep windows and doors closed because of heavy smoke. The brigade said the fire is believed to have been accidental.

stories.head: Timms review calls Pip process 'not fit for purpose' but proposes no cuts
stories.say: The first review of the Personal Independence Payment since it began calls the assessment process not fit for purpose. It proposes fast-track awards for terminal and severe conditions.
stories.stand: Sir Stephen Timms's review covers about 4 million claimants; the government has committed to reform with a response in the New Year.
body: The Timms review of Personal Independence Payment, published on Tuesday, says the assessment process is not fit for purpose. It is the first review of the disability benefit since it began in 2013 and covers England and Wales.

It recommends fast-track awards for terminal illness and severe conditions unlikely to change, and new questions about claimants' extra costs. It proposes no benefit cuts, though some claimants may lose money in a rebalancing.
About 4 million people claim Pip, and spending is forecast to pass £40bn by 2030. The government has committed to reform, with a detailed response expected in the New Year.

stories.say: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match ban has been overturned on appeal, so he can play against Brentford on Saturday.
stories.stand: Yoro was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak in Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
body: The Football Association overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension on Tuesday, after the club appealed against a wrongful dismissal.
Yoro was sent off in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday for fouling Alexander Isak. The referee ruled he had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.
He is now available for United's home Premier League game against Brentford on Saturday.

stories.head: Verstappen leads fight for second place ahead of Qatar Grand Prix
stories.say: With Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes already champions, the Qatar Grand Prix this weekend is about second place, where Max Verstappen leads Lewis Hamilton by thirty-seven points.
stories.stand: The 57-lap race at Lusail is on Sunday; Russell and Norris are three points behind Hamilton.
body: The Qatar Grand Prix runs at Lusail from 27 to 29 November, with the 57-lap race on Sunday. Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes have already won the drivers' and constructors' titles.
Antonelli has 402 points. Max Verstappen is second on 304, 37 ahead of Lewis Hamilton on 267, with George Russell and Lando Norris on 264.
Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren are fighting for second in the constructors' standings. Sergio Pérez will start from the back of the grid because of a penalty.
